purpose: Define monokl's ranking core -- identifier tokenizing, BM25 scoring, node-type and coverage boosts, deterministic ranking, and overlap dedup -- per docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Sections 6 (tokenize/tokenize_source only), 8 and 9, with the tie-break that Section 29 tenet #4 claims but Section 8's code omits (docs/architecture/query-and-ranking.md finding #9). These are pure functions over in-memory blocks; text search and the pipeline that feeds them are separate tracks.
scope: crates/monokl/src/tokens.rs (STOP_WORDS, tokenize, tokenize_source); crates/monokl/src/rank/{mod,bm25,boost,tokenize_doc}.rs (round6, score, coverage_boost, node_type_boost, tokenize_block, rank_blocks); crates/monokl/src/dedup.rs (dedup_blocks).
non_goals: Token counting with tiktoken (Section 6's count functions). Per Part 8 §7.5 it belongs to the budgeting layer, not core.
Text search, candidate selection and regex compilation (Section 7; SPEC-013).
Budgeting and truncation (Section 10). Part 8 §7.5 moves them out of core.
Document-frequency computation. rank_blocks takes df as an argument; who builds it belongs to the search pipeline track.
Changing BM25 constants, boost values or the score formula. They are carried over from Section 8 unchanged.

api_surface.name: tokens::tokenize
api_surface.description: Splits one identifier into lowercase sub-words per Section 6's case-transition rules, dropping tokens shorter than 2 characters and stop words.

api_surface.name: tokens::tokenize_source
api_surface.description: Splits source text on non-[A-Za-z0-9_] characters and tokenizes each fragment, keeping duplicates for term frequency.

api_surface.name: rank::score
api_surface.signature: pub fn score<S: BuildHasher>(doc_tokens: &[String], query_terms: &[&str], avg_doc_len: f64, corpus_size: usize, df: &HashMap<String, usize, S>) -> f64
api_surface.description: Okapi BM25, K1 = 1.5, B = 0.5, rounded with round6.

api_surface.name: rank::coverage_boost
api_surface.description: Fraction of matched_lines inside [line_start, line_end], rounded with round6; 0 when matched_lines is empty.

api_surface.name: rank::tokenize_block
api_surface.description: tokenize_source of the block's code followed by tokenize_source of its signature, if any.

api_surface.name: rank::rank_blocks
api_surface.signature: pub fn rank_blocks<S: BuildHasher>(blocks: Vec<(CodeBlock, Vec<String>)>, query_terms: &[&str], df: &HashMap<String, usize, S>) -> Vec<RankedBlock>
api_surface.description: Scores every block, sorts with the total order in AC-009, and assigns 1-based ranks.

api_surface.name: dedup::dedup_blocks
api_surface.description: Drops a block that overlaps an earlier kept block in the same file by more than half of the smaller block, then reassigns 1-based ranks.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: tokenize follows Section 6's transition rules exactly: tokenize("XMLParser") == ["xml", "parser"]; tokenize("getUserName") == ["user", "name"] ("get" is a stop word); tokenize("v8Engine") == ["v8", "engine"] (letter-to-digit never breaks); tokenize("user_id") == ["user", "id"]; tokenize("") == [].

tokenize drops tokens of length below 2 and every entry of Section 6's STOP_WORDS list, including the post-research additions crate, self, super, dyn, async, await and unsafe; non-ASCII characters act as separators.
tokenize_source keeps duplicates in source order: tokenize_source("fooBar(fooBar)") == ["foo", "bar", "foo", "bar"].
round6 rounds half away from zero at 6 decimal places (f64::round semantics): round6(0.1234565) and round6(1.0000004) give 0.123457 and 1.0.

score returns 0.0 when query_terms or doc_tokens is empty, skips terms with zero term frequency, and otherwise returns round6 of the sum over terms of ln((N - df + 0.5)/(df + 0.5) + 1) * tf*(K1+1)/(tf + K1*(1 - B + B*doc_len/avg_doc_len)), K1 = 1.5, B = 0.5. A hand-computed case (one doc of 4 tokens, avg_doc_len 4, N = 2, df = 1, tf = 2) is asserted to the exact round6 value.

node_type_boost returns exactly: Function 1.5; Class, Method, Constructor 1.4; Interface, Struct 1.3; TypeAlias, Enum 1.2; Variable, Impl 1.1; Property, Field, Macro 1.0; Module 0.9; Other 0.7 -- with no wildcard arm, so a new SymbolKind variant fails to compile until it is given a value.

coverage_boost is 0.0 for empty matched_lines, 1.0 when every matched line is within [line_start, line_end], and round6(inside / total) otherwise (e.g. 1 of 3 inside gives 0.333333). A block with line_end < line_start contains no lines and never panics.

rank_blocks returns an empty Vec for empty input; otherwise one RankedBlock per input with bm25_score, coverage_boost and node_type_boost set as above, final_score = round6(bm25 * node_type_boost + coverage_boost), parent_context None, and rank 1..=n in output order.

rank_blocks orders by a total order: final_score descending (f64::total_cmp), then file ascending, then line_start ascending, then line_end ascending. Two inputs that are permutations of each other produce identical output, so the order never depends on input order. This implements Section 29 tenet #4's (file, line_start) tie-break that Section 8's single-key sort lacked.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: query-and-ranking.md finding #9 requires either implementing the tenet or striking it; determinism is a stated principle, so it is implemented, with line_end added so blocks sharing a start line also order deterministically.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: dedup_blocks keeps the first block and drops any later block in the same file whose overlap with a kept block is more than half the smaller block's line count (overlap_lines * 2 > smaller_len); blocks in different files never dedupe; adjacent blocks with no shared line are both kept; ranks are reassigned 1..=n.
dedup_blocks never panics on a block with line_end < line_start; such a block has length 1 for the comparison (Section 9's saturating_sub).

reasoning: Everything except the sort order is carried over from Sections 6, 8 and 9. AC-009 is the one decision: the tie-break tenet #4 claims is implemented, since Part 8 and PRINCIPLES.md treat determinism as a requirement. total_cmp replaces partial_cmp so a NaN score cannot make the order input-dependent.
